title: AMD Instinct Coder 355 Launches as On-Prem AI Coding Box
summary: AMD, Supermicro, Dell and Spectro Cloud launch Instinct Coder 355 at KubeCon 2026, an on-prem AI coding appliance with MI355X GPUs supporting 50 developers.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- AMD and partners launched Instinct Coder 355 at KubeCon NA 2026, a turnkey on-prem coding appliance with eight MI355X GPUs.
- Each appliance runs GLM-5.3 locally, supports roughly 50 concurrent developers, and routes overflow to cloud frontier models.
- Spectro Cloud claims up to 75% lower token costs versus external services and 98% of frontier-model benchmark performance.


AMD, Supermicro, Dell, and Spectro Cloud have officially launched the Instinct Coder 355, a turnkey on-premises AI coding appliance designed to serve enterprise development teams without round-trip latency to external cloud services. Announced November 10, 2026 at KubeCon North America in Salt Lake City, the appliance pairs eight AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs with a Dell PowerEdge XE9785 server running GLM-5.3 inference locally, and Spectro Cloud claims one box can handle approximately 50 concurrent developers.


The pitch is straightforward: keep sensitive code and inference workloads inside the firewall, reduce token costs by up to 75% compared to cloud frontier models, and route overflow tasks to external providers only when the local model reaches its limits. Orders open through Spectro Cloud and authorized resellers, with live demonstrations scheduled at the vendor's KubeCon booth.


## Release date and availability


Officially launched on November 10, 2026 at KubeCon North America, the Instinct Coder 355 is available for order through Spectro Cloud and its reseller network. The vendor held live demonstrations at Booth 125 throughout the three-day conference and has not disclosed list pricing or lead times in the public announcement.


## Hardware specifications


Each Instinct Coder 355 node stacks eight AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs, each delivering 288 GB of HBM3E memory and up to 8 TB/s memory bandwidth. The Dell PowerEdge XE9785 chassis houses the GPU array alongside a pair of AMD EPYC 9575F 64-core CPUs and 3 TB of DDR5 system RAM, according to Spectro Cloud's launch materials.


The appliance runs GLM-5.3 locally through Spectro Cloud's PaletteAI Inference Launchpad. When a coding task exceeds the capacity or capability of the on-premises model, PaletteAI routes the request to Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, or Google Gemini. The vendor describes this hybrid routing as a local-first architecture that balances performance, cost, and data residency requirements.


## Performance and cost claims


Spectro Cloud states the appliance reduces AI coding token costs by up to 75% versus cloud frontier models and achieves up to 98% of frontier-model benchmark performance. The vendor has not published the workload mix or third-party validation underlying those figures. One appliance is projected to support roughly 50 concurrent developers, though that capacity depends on the mix of autocomplete, code generation, and conversational queries in actual use.


The company references its earlier Instinct Coder 325 as proof that enterprises prefer local-first AI coding paths and that open-weight models handle most day-to-day work. Co-founder and CEO Tenry Fu said in the announcement that customers now choose appliances tailored to their specific capacity and compliance needs.


## Market context


The Instinct Coder 355 arrives in a crowded week for silicon and infrastructure announcements. It joins a growing shelf of private coding-assistant appliances that aim to keep inference, training data, and proprietary source code behind the corporate firewall. The appliance competes directly with cloud-based tools like GitHub Copilot and Cursor, as well as other on-premises offerings from silicon vendors and systems integrators.


Enterprise adoption of[AI-assisted coding](https://emergent.sh/glossary/ai-assisted-coding) has accelerated sharply in 2026, driven by developer productivity gains and executive concern over sending proprietary code to third-party APIs. The vendor's claim of 75% cost reduction reflects the economics of amortizing GPU capital expenditure across dozens of developers, compared to per-token charges from external providers.


## What this means


The launch signals AMD's continued push into enterprise AI inference, particularly in verticals where data residency and latency matter more than access to the absolute frontier of model capability. By bundling hardware, software orchestration, and hybrid routing into a single SKU, Spectro Cloud lowers the integration burden for IT buyers who lack in-house ML infrastructure expertise. The appliance model also shifts the cost structure from variable OpEx to fixed CapEx, a trade-off that favors organizations with stable, predictable developer headcount and coding workloads that fit within the performance envelope of open-weight models.
